newsitem.title: USA: CMS hits record power demand on Mich. heat.
newsitem.headline: CMS hits record power demand on Mich. heat.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Monday its peak electricity demand set a record high of 7,304 megawatts (MW) at 1400 EDT today due to the heat wave stretching across the Midwest and Northeast.
This beats the previous record of 7,167 MW set last August 7, a company spokesman said.
At 1500 EDT Monday, peak demand had eased to about 7,298 MW, but the spokesman added that the previous record had been set at 1700 EDT.

To curb the usage of electricity and avoid interruptions in service, Consumers has asked its customers to reduce their use of air conditioning and "any non-essential electrical appliances," the spokesman said.
The CMS Energy Corp subsidiary serves natural gas and electricity to more than six million of Michigan's 9.5 million residents.
Temperatures in Detroit surpassed the 90 degree F mark today but are expected to slip into the high-80s on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to Weather Services Corp.
